newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Suspected insider trading in Foreningsbanken. [CORRECTED 09:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Suspected insider trading in Foreningsbanken. [CORRECTED 09:40 GMT]

text.p: Sweden's Financial Supervisory Board (FI) said on Thursday that it had reported suspected insider trading in shares of Swedish regional bank Foreningsbanken (corrects headline and text to make clear the suspicions relate to the shares in the bank) in 1996 to the state prosecutor.
"The Financial Supervisory Board has found reason to suspect that insider trading rules over forbidden trade have been broken," it said in a statement.
FI said it reported the matter to the state prosecutor's special division for economic crimes.
"The case involves three people who are suspected of crime related to illegal trade," it said.
Foreningsbanken is a regional bank owned primarily by the Swedish Farmers' Union (LRF).
